summary.headline: Jyoti CNC Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 37% to INR509 crore, but consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin slipped to 23.4% on Huron revenue deferral.
summary.overview:
Standalone revenue grew 37% YoY to INR509 crore with adjusted EBITDA margin of 28.4% and PAT of INR88 crore (17.2% margin). Consolidated revenue was INR508.5 crore (+24% YoY), but Huron revenue was deferred because the company moved from percentage-of-completion to recognising revenue only on dispatch, citing end-user certificate and export licence delays. Consolidated adjusted EBITDA was INR119 crore (23.4%) after a INR10 crore unrealised forex loss; reported EBITDA was INR109 crore (21.4%). Management guided to 25-30% top-line growth and about 25% EBITDA margin for FY27, with the 10,000-machine expansion due by end-September.</overview>

segments.name: Standalone (Jyoti India)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR509 crore (+37% YoY), adjusted EBITDA margin 28.4%, PAT INR88 crore. Management says standalone margin was about 27.5% after Huron effect. Demand from general engineering, automotive, EMS, defence and precision engineering.

segments.name: Huron (Germany, subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Produced about EUR6.5 million of machines in Q1 but billed about EUR3 million; roughly INR35 crore of revenue deferred versus Q1 FY26 (about INR70 crore). Management says costs are fully booked, so the gap hits margin. Recognition moved from percentage-of-completion to dispatch-based.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth guided at 25-30%; EBITDA margin guided around 25%, which management says it is committed to.
Huron FY27 revenue expected at INR300-325 crore, with Huron EBITDA margin of 8-10%; management says Huron will be PAT positive this year.
Standalone FY27 capex about INR200-225 crore against a total expansion target of about INR450 crore for the new capacity; management said capex will not touch INR300 crore.
Debt to stay at about March 2026 levels; management targets net debt not above 2x EBITDA. OCF for FY27 expected at about 50% of EBITDA.
Order book expected to reach INR2,500-3,000 crore by year-end; FY27 machine volume expected above 8,000 units.
capex_capacity: New 10,000-machine-per-year facility targeted to commence operations by end-September 2026; machine shop, sheet metal and paint shop buildings ready or near completion, with foundry about one month late (October).
Current capacity 6,000 machines per year; 5,550 machines built in FY26; Q1 FY27 utilisation 86%.
Management cites a targeted INR450 crore capex for the new capacity and says it is on track.
CNC controller: HMI ready; commercialisation expected in about two years; PLI application filed with capital subsidy about 25% central plus matching state support (about 50% total).
Raw material and inventory built up over the past nine months to support the ramp-up; management expects working capital and inventory to improve after the new facility is operational.
demand_pricing: Order book INR4,848 crore; mix: aerospace and defence 38%, general engineering 20%, automotive 19%, EMS 13%, die and mould 4%.
Q1 revenue mix: aerospace and defence 37%, automotive 35%, general engineering 17%, EMS 6%, other 5%.
Blended realisation about INR34.56 lakh per machine in Q1 FY27 vs INR34.41 lakh in Q1 FY26; management expects the range to hold.
Management says the Rajkot unit booked more than 250 machines in July and that the company crossed 1,000 machines in one month in the domestic market.

India imports about 60-62% of machine tool demand, mainly from Japan, Europe and South Korea. New NX double-column machine targets railway, commercial vehicles, infra, power and heavy engineering, with 6m model launched and 8m and 10m in development.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Huron's accounting change and what drove the revenue gap?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says end-user certificates (EUC) and export licences now take longer, and auditors apply a conservative dispatch-based approach. Revenue will return to POCM once EUC is received; the company says it can book POCM if EUC arrives within 3 months of order. Around 7-8 machines across multiple orders are pending, and management expects clearance in one batch.

qa_highlights.question: Is there an impairment risk if the Huron investigation drags on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no impairment risk ("Not at all").

qa_highlights.question: Will the Huron revenue shortfall reverse in the coming quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Q2 dispatches to improve, but says large machines have long lead times, so the bulk should come in Q3 and Q4. Management said the company should be judged on an annual basis, not quarterly.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 capex and debt plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone capex of INR200-225 crore for FY27 against a INR450 crore expansion total. Debt is expected to stay flat versus March; management targets net debt not above 2x EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Why did interest cost rise and why was it not capitalised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said costs were booked to P&L because the new capacity has already been put to use (building and components), so capitalisation was not applied.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected FY27 Huron margin and does it reach PAT positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Huron FY27 revenue expected at INR300-325 crore with EBITDA margin of 8-10%; management said Huron is PAT positive this year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the sequential margin decline explained by Huron alone?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes; it pointed to the same standalone business at about 27.5% margin in Q1.
